title: The complete guide to LiveKit Agents

title: How to compile JavaScript into a single executable
partialText: Turn a JavaScript program into one executable file, like Go and Rust do, with deno compile, bun build --compile and Node.js single executable apps.

title: Use WhatCable to figure out what your USB cable can do
partialText: WhatCable is a free, open source Mac app that reads the chip inside a USB-C cable and tells you its real data speed, power rating and what limits it.

title: How to avoid the "Open Anyway" message when building macOS apps
partialText: macOS blocks apps downloaded from the internet until people click Open Anyway. Sign your app with a Developer ID and notarize it, and it opens normally.

title: What happens when AI agents shop for us
partialText: Shopify wants Muse to check out with Shop Pay on every store. I want the agent to find the product. I still want a person to approve the exact charge.

title: Use npkill to find and delete old node_modules folders
partialText: npkill is a free terminal tool that finds every node_modules folder on your computer, shows its size and age, and deletes the ones you pick.

title: I built Repo Foyer, a Chrome extension that puts my repos on the GitHub home page
partialText: Repo Foyer is my free, open source Chrome extension that replaces the GitHub home page with your repositories, so you can jump to the one you're working on.

title: I open sourced testvm, so your coding agents can test Mac apps in a VM
partialText: testvm is my free, open source tool that runs Mac app builds in a headless macOS VM, so coding agents test them without taking over your screen.

title: I built Footage Ferry, a Mac app to import Blackmagic Camera videos
partialText: Footage Ferry is my free, open source Mac app that copies Blackmagic Camera clips from an iPhone over USB, checks every copy byte for byte, and then offers to delete the originals.

title: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK
partialText: How to use Jev with the Vercel AI SDK: install the TypeSafe provider, call experimental_evaluate, read confidence, use AI Gateway, and compare Jev with an LLM.

title: I built Chip Pops, 6,000 8-bit sound effects for my apps
partialText: Chip Pops is my free, open source Mac app and command line tool with about 6,000 8-bit sound effects made with jsfxr. Click a sound to hear it, drag it into your app.

title: I built Couch Snake, the classic phone game for the Apple TV
partialText: Couch Snake is my free, open source Apple TV game: the classic snake game from old mobile phones, full screen on a green LCD board, steered by swiping on the Siri Remote.

title: How to use cf, the new Cloudflare CLI
partialText: Learn cf, the new Cloudflare CLI: find commands with cf cli search, configure Workers in cloudflare.config.ts, deploy, and migrate from Wrangler.

title: Hosting picker: find where to host your app
partialText: Answer four questions and get three hosts that fit your project, with a monthly price and the main catch. 21 providers, prices checked October 1, 2026.

title: Payment picker: find how to get paid for your app
partialText: Find a payment provider for your product, compare fees on your own numbers, and see who handles tax and disputes. Merchant of Record and direct providers.

title: A deep dive into cron
partialText: Learn cron on Linux and macOS: crontab syntax, schedules, the cron environment, logs, overlapping runs, time zones, launchd and systemd timers.

title: I built Architecture Dissector, a Mac app that shows how my apps are built
partialText: Architecture Dissector is my free, open source Mac app that draws how your apps are built, their workflows and the data they store, from maps your coding agents write.

title: I built Slide Lookout, a Chrome extension that shows your next slide
partialText: Slide Lookout is my free, open source Chrome extension that shows the next slide of a Notion presentation in a small floating window, on top of the fullscreen slides.

title: How my Mac apps update themselves from GitHub Releases
partialText: Tranquillity Maker and CLI Tools Cabinet check GitHub once a day, download the new release, verify it, and replace themselves. Here's how it works, in one Swift file with no dependencies.

title: How to let coding agents test Mac apps in a VM
partialText: Run a headless macOS VM with Tart so coding agents can launch, screenshot and click through your Mac apps without taking over your screen.

title: Should you pay for the Apple Developer Program?

title: How to fix "Stacked PRs are not enabled for this repository"
partialText: Stacked PRs are not enabled for this repository is a gh stack warning with no setting to flip. Check your gh account and repo, or open regular PRs.

title: How to use Jev confidence scores
partialText: How to use Jev confidence scores to decide when code acts, asks for confirmation, or hands off to a person, with thresholds tuned on labeled data.

partialText: VM Peek is my free, open source Mac app that shows what coding agents do in a macOS test VM: its screen live, which agents are using it and for what, and every command they ran.

partialText: Post Slide Deck is my free, open source Mac app and Chrome extension that turn posts on X into slides. Click the slide icon under a post, reorder the slides, and play them in the app window while you record.

title: How to classify text with Jev

title: What is poteto-mode in pstack?
partialText: poteto-mode is the pstack router skill for Cursor. Describe a result and it picks a playbook, calls the other skills, delegates to models and verifies the work.
